Lina (People Ops): Heads-up: we added SRE-friendly examples to the OKR + self-review kit today. Link: https://redwoodinference.docs/hr/okr-sre-examples-2026
Raj (SRE Manager): Great. Can you post a 2-line manager checklist I can drop in our on-call playbook?
Lina (People Ops): Yup — 2-line checklist you can paste:
1) Limit team OKRs to 3 primary priorities, each with an owner and a measurable signal (use proxy metrics if needed).
2) Ensure every direct adds a 1-page self-review + 1 development goal; managers add a 1-2 sentence summary and suggested rating, plus calibration date.
people-ops-bot: Reminder: self-reviews open 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC; deadline 2026-04-10 09:00 UTC.
Hannah (SRE): For SREs: examples for operational vs project goals? Our work mixes incidents + long-term infra.
Lina (People Ops): Two compact examples you can copy:
````
Operational OKR (Committed): Reduce production p99 errors by 30%
- Owner: SRE team
- Signal: weekly incident count; mean-time-to-detect (MTTD)
Project OKR (Committed): Migrate inference fleet to new KV cache
- Owner: Raj
- Milestone Q1: Proof-of-concept + perf tests (signal: canary p99 improvement)
- Milestone Q2: Rollout to 2 regions (signal: errors <= target)
````
Marcus (Eng Manager): Any guidance on how to write the manager summary when an on-call rotation caused delays?
Lina (People Ops): Short recommended phrasing:
"Work impacted by on-call rotation and production incident X; engineering tradeoffs documented. Delivered Y features and progressed migration milestones. Suggested rating: Meets with note on incident response contributions."
Raj (SRE Manager): Can we get a micro self-review starter tuned for SREs?
Lina (People Ops): Copyable SRE starter:
````
What I owned this quarter (2-4 bullets; link to runbooks/dashboards)
Operational impact (incidents reduced, MTTx improvements, pager load)
Project progress (milestones reached, perf numbers)
Key blockers & mitigations (on-call load, infra limits)
Next quarter focus + 1 skill goal (e.g., observability, capacity planning)
Support needed from manager (time, approvals, infra credits)
````
Hannah (SRE): How strict are Committed vs Stretch labels? We have a hard time predicting incident load.
Lina (People Ops): Use Committed for what you reasonably plan to complete given current capacity; Stretch is upside. For ops teams, document assumptions (e.g., expected on-call weeks) in the goal note. Managers should calibrate if assumptions change.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Rubric please — short and pasteable for managers.
Lina (People Ops): Rubric (one-liners to paste):
- Exceeds: Delivered outcomes beyond plan with measurable impact; strong collaboration and ownership.
- Meets: Delivered planned outcomes or acceptable progress with clear context.
- Needs Improvement: Missed key outcomes without documented, reasonable blockers; manager plan required.
Also for SREs: add an "Operational Excellence" callout when incident response and reliability work are primary contributions.
